newsitem.title: FRANCE: Danone chief eyes long-term sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Danone chief eyes long-term sales growth.

text.p: The chairman of French food firm Groupe Danone predicted in a newspaper interview on Monday that sales should jump to between 100 and 120 billion francs within five to ten years.
"From a current 80 billion francs, sales should reach 100 or 120 billion francs, of which 30 percent (generated) outside Europe," Franck Riboud told daily Le Figaro.
He was commenting on the sales picture within five to ten years.
Riboud also reiterated his forecast of a six percent full-year net profit rise in 1996. Danone posted a 1995 net attributable profit of 2.13 billion francs.
A 1.8 billion francs provision set aside in 1995 and involving mostly restructurings in Europe should allow Danone to make savings of some one billion francs, he said.
Riboud also denied recurring rumours that Danone was considering selling its beer business.

He stressed the beer business was a large contributor to the group's profit and that Danone was in fact developing its beer operations, having recently acquired a brewery in China and beer distribution networks in France.
